text:
maria_support: Hey team — incoming customer escalation from AcmeChat on Dedicated. They see sudden 429s and tail latency spikes starting ~08:12 UTC. They say traffic pattern didn't change on their side. Can someone triage? :eyes:

devon_runtime: grabbing pool and tenant details now. Which pool?

maria_support: Pool: ded-gpu-eu-west-2-3, tenant_id: acme-prod-42. They attached a few example request IDs: r_01F6A, r_01F6B. Customer reports error body: `\{"error\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\",\"retry_after\":2\}` even though their console quota shows 20k units/min.

ira_sre: quick check of tenant rate table shows a weird entry: acme-prod-42 -> quota_units=20000, unit_type="requests_per_minute" in UI but the enforcement layer is reading `tokens_per_minute`. That mismatch can cause token-heavy requests (embeddings + long completions) to trigger 429s. Repro: I ran a short script mimicking their burst and got 429s at ~1.6k requests.

alex_prodeng: omg that explains it — the quota migration job we rolled last week converted some tenants but left unit_type unset for ones with legacy billing flag. Looks like acme got the unset value which defaulted to tokens in enforcement.

maria_support: Customer was using long prompt templates, so token usage had spiky distribution. So enforcement saw them as over-quota. Can we temporarily exempt them while we fix the mapping? They flagged this as P1.

devon_runtime: Ops-bot, open incident for tenant quota mismatch?

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-379 — "dedicated tenant quota enforcement mismatch (acme-prod-42)". Paging oncall.

ira_sre: Mitigation options: 1) update enforcement table to reflect UI unit_type=requests for tenant (fast, low-risk); 2) flip customer to a higher quota profile; 3) add short-lived override until migration script is corrected. I can apply (1) now if we agree.

alex_prodeng: We should do (1) + schedule rollback window. Also file a PR to fix migration. I'll own that.

devon_runtime: Before changing, let's confirm autoscaler behavior: logs show no new pods because autoscaler evaluated CPU/GPU metrics, not request queue length — because queueing is upstream of runtime where throttle denies requests. So autoscaling wouldn't have helped.

maria_support: Customer also reported increased latency on successful requests (200s) around same time. Any link to throttling?

ira_sre: Yes — when enforcement layer rejects tokens as 429, client retries with backoff causing hotspots and bursts. Some retries also queue and push healthy requests into longer tails. Also we saw KV-cache pressure due to partial requests. Noted in logs: `enforce_rate_limit: token_budget < 0 -> reject`.

devon_runtime: I'll patch the enforcement table now (apply statement):
```
UPDATE tenant_rate_limits
SET unit_type = 'requests_per_minute'
WHERE tenant_id = 'acme-prod-42' AND unit_type IS NULL;
```
Then flush in-memory cache: `curl -X POST https://runtime.internal/cache/flush?tenant=acme-prod-42`

maria_support: Please notify customer before/after. I'll send interim note: "We're investigating and may apply a temporary config change; expect a short window of reduced throttles."

ira_sre: Patch applied, cache flushed. Monitoring now.

ops-bot: Alert suppressed for INC-2026-379 for 30m.
devon_runtime: Early signs look good — 429s dropped to baseline, tail latency recovering. P95 for 1m window down from 2.6s to 480ms.

maria_support: Customer acked: "Thanks — looks good on our end, throughput normalized." They asked what caused it and how to prevent recurrence.

alex_prodeng: Root cause: migration script left unit_type null for tenants with legacy billing flags, enforcement defaults to token units, mismatch with UI. Fix: ship migration patch + add validation in admin UI and create a canary run for large tenant migrations. I'll open PR and include a DB constraint.

ira_sre: Follow-ups: 1) Add metric for `unit_type_mismatch_count` and alert when >0 after migrations. 2) Make autoscaler consider queued request length upstream (tickets filed). 3) Communicate RCA to ACME and include recommended client-side retry/backoff guidance.

maria_support: I'll send ACME the RCA draft and close the support ticket once PR merged. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

devon_runtime: +1. Logging final note: `enforce_rate_limit` traces show decision path and the null->tokens default. We'll reconcile and add a migration verification step.

alex_prodeng: I'll add the DB constraint and a migration verification runbook. Targeting hotfix today and full rollout in next deploy window.

maria_support: Closing thread here after follow-up. If anyone wants to add notes for the RCA doc, drop them in #eng-postmortems.
